confAdapterId.description:
This is the optional adapterId of the running adapter that contains configuration related objects. This property can only be specified in the type=application entry of the conf file.

The runtime /afw/_AdaptiveApplication_/current object will consist of properties from the type=application entry of the conf file plus unique properties from the optional /<confAdapterId>/_AdaptiveConf_application/<applicationId> object.

All services defined by _AdaptiveServiceConf_ objects in <confAdapterId> with startup 'permanent' or 'immediate' will be started when the type=application conf entry is processed.

additionalProperties.description: Maps a logical path prefix to a host directory for open_file(), compile_from_file(), and eval_from_file(). The property name is the prefix: a logical path must equal the property name or begin with the property name followed by '/'. Among matching prefixes, the longest wins (so property 'includes' is preferred over 'include' for path 'includes/a.as'). The property value is a template for the host directory, evaluated when the application conf is processed (plain strings are unchanged; substitutions such as environment:: may be used). The evaluated path is resolved to a full path at that time (relative paths use the process current working directory). The resolved host path must remain under that directory after canonicalization; path segments of '..' and other escapes are rejected. Example: property 'my' with value '/temp/my' allows open_file('s1', 'my/xyz', 'w') to open host file '/temp/my/xyz' when that path stays under '/temp/my'.

qualifiedVariables.description:
The name of each property in this object corresponds to a qualifier that is available in processing associated with this application. The qualifier can not be an empty string. The properties of these 'qualifier objects' are template values that are accessible as qualified variables. These variables are evaluated once per execution context (xctx) as they are accessed.

Some qualifiers are restricted.
